agent.problem: The only setup is that Jesus refers to 'a time long ago.' Noah, Moses and Abraham all fit that description, so the baker cannot reason out Noah and must guess wording he has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The opening 'that servant' depends on the preceding story card to identify the faithful and wise servant. Since that card is no longer visible, the question needs to identify the servant and his assignment within its own wording.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The earlier cards establish that the servant is wicked, but they do not establish that he beats rather than mocks his fellow servants, or that he eats and drinks with drunkards rather than priests or strangers. Both blanks therefore ask the baker to guess unseen verse wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points specifically to hypocrites rather than drunkards or tax collectors. The baker can only guess the unseen wording of verse 51.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
